verdict.rationale: Reader is a stateless HTTP API, so scaling means firing many parallel requests. Several items support that use: a hosted proxy pool that rotates residential and datacenter IPs and handles anti-bot challenges (gh-9), a prebuilt self-hostable container with headless Chrome for running your own capacity (gh-8), and S3-backed caching reused across requests (gh-20). Nothing in the evidence documents concurrency limits, rate limits, batch submission or session management, and a community commenter notes the website does not mention API limits (comm-1). missing for 10: documented concurrency and rate limits, a batch or bulk scraping endpoint, horizontal-scaling guidance for self-hosting, independent evidence of high-volume concurrent use.
